top_choice_rationale: P002 rests on a compact, analytically transparent model (Bistritzer-MacDonald) that predicted a specific, falsifiable magic angle near 1.1 degrees, which an experiment then confirmed with correlated insulating and superconducting states, so the flat-band mechanism is understood and the result has been reproduced across laboratories and moire platforms. The open pairing mechanism, the young age of the field and the credit problem (Cao, early twisted-bilayer theory) are real weaknesses, but the citation can be scoped to the magic-angle flat bands and observed phases. P001 is a close second: a clean two-name allocation and a settled, widely reproduced experimental claim with a simple general mechanism, and I would move it first if a record check shows the early flat-band work has a stronger claim on the magic-angle result. A prize in either case is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no collaboration with any candidate, only the general Gothenburg physics link to Chalmers colleagues
